# Re-engage open deals: Outlook & Notion

**Pattern:** Reminders & Follow-ups · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across Outlook and Notion.

It moves through 8 working steps, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Slot Free?
3. Record Booking
4. Send Confirmation (Outlook)
5. Propose Alternative Slots
6. Hold Until Reminder Time
7. Send Reminder (Outlook)
8. Save Execution Metadata

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Slot Free? → Record Booking → Send Confirmation (Outlook) → Propose Alternative Slots → Hold Until Reminder Time → Send Reminder (Outlook) → Save Execution Metadata

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Outlook and Notion aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Outlook
- Newsletters work where "Slot Free?" is still a manual step before Outlook
- Newsletters work that only reaches Outlook on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Outlook and Notion in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Outlook or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 8 nodes in this newsletters build
- The pause before Outlook is durable — a newsletters run survives a restart
- Every newsletters run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Outlook
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 8 nodes for newsletters before wiring Outlook

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Availability is checked *before* booking, not assumed — creating an event unconditionally would double-book the same slot if two requests arrive close together. The confirmation and the later reminder are separate sends because they serve different moments: confirming intent now, and cutting no-shows right before the appointment.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Change the reminder lead time from 1 hour to 24 hours.
2. Simulate two near-simultaneous booking requests for the same slot and see which gets the alternative-slots branch.
3. Add a cancellation path that frees the slot back up.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
